messages:
sarah-cs: Heads up — large EU customer seeing spikes in latency (~700-1200ms) and intermittent 403s for inference requests since ~08:20 UTC. They say requests are getting routed to us-east despite setting region=eu-west in their headers. They attached request IDs.

jess: link to logs? request ids? we can check routing table.

sarah-cs: pasted one example: req=01F3ZQ1X user=acme-corp id=rcpt-9b2a
curl -v 'https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate' \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \\n  -H 'x-client-region: eu-west-1' \\n  -H 'x-request-id: rcpt-9b2a'
response: 200 -> 403 (after ~820ms) in some traces; envoy->upstream shows route chosen = us-east-pool-3.

omar: that's odd. last deploy touched gateway L7 header handling (rollout at 08:15) — maybe header inheritance change.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-17T08:14:42Z by kevin — envoy-gateway:add-header-inheritance-flag v2 -> rolling to prod (canary 10%).

kevin: I rolled a change that toggles "preserve_external_headers" to true to keep arbitrary incoming headers for debugging. It was supposed to be behind a feature flag but the canary config accidentally flipped for all gateways for the new envoy cluster.

jess: suspect: when preserve_external_headers=true, Envoy appends incoming region headers instead of replacing, so if upstream fallback rewrite sets x-client-region=us-east, we end up with both values or stale one wins at route decision time. That could cause route selection to use wrong precedence.

linda: I see traces where upstream auth checks expect audience==eu, but Host header got rewritten to us-east host earlier in pipeline. Auth library checks `aud: host` -> mismatch -> 403.

mike-oncall: repro steps I just ran from my laptop (eu build):
1) curl -v -H 'x-client-region: eu-west-1' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
2) check envoy access log on gw-eu-1: `kubectl logs gateway-eu-1 -c envoy --since=5m | grep rcpt-9b2a`
3) notice header set sequence: incoming `x-client-region: eu-west-1` -> gateway appended `x-client-region: us-east-1` -> route matched on last header value 'us-east-1'

jess: can you paste the exact access log line? we need :authority and x-client-region fields.

mike-oncall: log: `ts=2026-03-17T08:22:31Z tid=rcpt-9b2a method=POST path=/v1/generate :authority=api.redwood-inference.com upstream=us-east-pool-3 x-client-region="eu-west-1,us-east-1" user=acme-corp status=403 latency_ms=827`

omar: that header value format (comma list) is Envoy's append behavior. route matcher probably uses the last token which is us-east-1. This explains cross-region routing and extra latency.

kevin: confirmed — the canary inadvertently flipped a global flag in our Helm values. Rolling it back now.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated 2026-03-17T08:31:05Z for envoy-gateway -> rolling to all clusters.

sarah-cs: customer is asking for timeline and mitigation. They want a hotfix because their SLA is impacted.

jess: mitigation options: 1) immediate rollback (in progress) 2) patch gateway config to `header_action: REPLACE` for x-client-region and Host rewrite (safer) 3) add a route matcher that normalizes multi-value headers and prefers first value. I prefer 1+2.

kevin: rollback should complete in ~5-10 mins, then we push a patch that sets explicit `header_action: replace` for the region header and Host rewrites. I'll also add an integration test that sends duplicate region headers and asserts correct route chosen.

linda: note — auth service also needs to be tolerant: stop using `Host` as single source of truth for audience until header normalization is done. I'll open a PR to add fallback and stricter logging.

mike-oncall: confirmed rollback completed at 08:37:10 UTC, canary -> 0%. I'm sending a smoke run.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete 2026-03-17T08:37:10Z for envoy-gateway.

mike-oncall: smoke: curl -v -H 'x-client-region: eu-west-1' ... -> route now hits eu pool (eu-pool-2) and latency back to 80-120ms. No 403 in 50 samples.

sarah-cs: told customer rollback done, will follow up with a postmortem and timeline for patch. They want a corrective PR and test.

jess: action items: kevin to push header_action=REPLACE patch + test (ETA today EOD), linda to harden auth audience parsing (ETA tomorrow), ops to add alert when x-client-region contains multiple tokens (low effort).

kevin: starting patch now, will tag as hotfix and notify once deployed.

sarah-cs: thanks team — customer relieved for now but wants writeup. I'll draft customer message after postmortem. :+1:

mike-oncall: creating incident ticket INC-2026-0317-004 and linking traces + logs.

jess: long-term we should avoid relying on mutable headers for routing. Put explicit region in token claims or use geo-ip fallback. Also add unit test to our gateway CI that simulates header-appending proxies.

sarah-cs: ok closing thread for now, will reopen if customer sees regression.
